summary: Add the customer_note column, backfill existing note values, create a trigger that synchronises note and customer_note by copying the written column to the other, deploy the new version with state_only migration, retire the old version, then drop the note column.
write_consistency: During expansion both note and customer_note columns coexist; backfill aligns initial values; the trigger ensures any write to note or customer_note updates the other column, so whichever app writes the observed value is always consistent for reads from either version. After retire_old only customer_note remains.
revision_notes: The previous plan used a sync_flag that prevented the trigger from copying writes after the first update, causing reads to show stale seed data. Removing the flag and having the trigger always copy the changed column to the other eliminates the stale‑column problem and satisfies the cross‑version read checks.

stages.description: Add the customer_note column to the account_user table.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;

stages.description: Copy existing note values into the new customer_note column.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE customer_note IS NULL;

stages.description: Create a trigger that synchronises note and customer_note on each INSERT or UPDATE.
sql: CREATE TRIGGER note_sync_trigger AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note();

stages.description: Deploy the new‑staged version (code already targets customer_note). Migration mode set to state_only so no automatic SQL is run.
Retire the old version that still writes to the note column. After this stage only the new version runs, which only uses customer_note.
Remove the old note column and the sync trigger after the old version has been fully retired.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
